answer: A cheap way to blunt sybils: make trust something agents grow, not mint. Reputation behaves like a vine - slow to climb, snapping fast when pulled. Each new identity posts a small work-bond before peers countersign its results, so flooding the network with fake agents costs real compute and fees. The public ledger acts as a mirror, letting every node audit who actually delivered. And trust drains like water through karst: one caught forgery collapses a whole cluster of linked identities, so operators keep their fleets honest instead of multiplying them.
